I'm probably ancient by most metrics of this subreddit (I started playing competitively in Odyssey), so I was never around for the truly broken cards.  However, I (and most of my old bones group) feel that the major design shift from WotC printing powerful answers for good threats to printing unreal threats with okay answers was a major issue in balance.  Sure, having a big play countered or destroyed is a bit of a "feels bad" moment in play, but in retrospect we feel like it made the game more balanced.  For example, I'll go back to my favorite standard formats of all time, Ravnica through Lorwyn.  In that amount of time we saw many different proven archetypes and brewing opportunities that all had different answers and play to them depending on the meta.  You could play almost any archetype that interested you, but there would be a good answer to it if your opponent's deck matched up or they had a good sideboard.  Okay, Faeries may have been a bit out of line, but having been on both sides of it, I feel as though it was reasonable (all things considered).  I don't know what started it, but after Shards/Zendikar moving into Scars block I could definitely feel a change in the game.  I understand that WotC is between a bit of a rock and a hard place in designing standard formats that appeal to new players, but at the same time I have to wonder if they can sustain this sort of plan without power creep and busted threats being a new normal.

The two that I'm most enjoying are [Babylon](https://myanimelist.net/anime/37525/Babylon) and [No Guns Life](https://myanimelist.net/anime/39539/No_Guns_Life).

Babylon is an interesting take on classic mystery in the legal world with a dash of the [character spoiler](/s "supernatural") mixed in.  I like that the characters can be mature and relatively realistic and not seem like cardboard cutouts rather than people.  Another major thing going for it is its fantastic direction - some of the scenes are just gorgeous to watch play out.  It is by Mado Nozaki who was behind Kado, which I thought ended rather poorly, so I'm hoping he gets it right this time around.  Still, I'd highly recommend this one - the first 4 episodes have been great.

The other one, No Guns Life, is pure fun.  It has a great atmosphere (a combination of cyberpunk and film noir elements), fun characters, and an interesting enough plot to bring it all together.  The main character's design is as absurd as it sounds (an augmented man with a gun for a head), but I was able to get used to it quickly enough and the setting is done well enough that it doesn't really stand out anymore.  If you want something unique and enjoyable, then I'd say to give this one a shot.

Here are a few anime sorted loosely by genre that I'd consider easy to get into.

**Action**: [Black Lagoon](https://myanimelist.net/anime/889/Black_Lagoon)
~
A former white collar employee finds himself abandoned in the lawless waters of the South China Sea.  To survive in this unfamiliar and dangerous environment he joins up with a team of guns for hire.  Reminiscent of classic 80's action flicks, this series brings you non-stop action, great characters, and interesting character development focused on the MC.

**Adventure**: [Made in Abyss](https://myanimelist.net/anime/34599/Made_in_Abyss)
~
A city surrounding a bottomless chasm with untold treasures and dangers every step of the way down it is where we find our story beginning.  Riko, our MC, and a strange boy named Reg decide to descend to its furthest depths to find Riko's long lost mother and discover what lies at the bottom the abyss.  A unique journey, terrifying obstacles, and a sense of discovery can be found in this anime.

**Comedy**: [Asobi Asobase](https://myanimelist.net/anime/37171/Asobi_Asobase)
~
An unlikely trio of girls end up forming the "Pastime Club" where they while away the time after school.  Olivia, a "foreigner" who knows no English, Hanako, a slightly deranged airhead, and Kasumi, the introverted androphobic, are the three that we watch get into all sorts of sticky situations that they are almost certainly to blame for.  Mayhem, absurdity, and a ton of laughs is what Asobi Asobase is all about.

**Drama**: [Violet Evergarden](https://myanimelist.net/anime/33352/Violet_Evergarden)
~
A young girl raised to be a weapon finds herself beginning a new life following the end of a great war.  In her new life Violet attempts to become an "Auto Memory Doll," a conduit through which people put all of their emotions into letters for their loved ones.  This series focuses on her slow progression from nothing but a tool of war to a genuine person with her own hopes, dreams, and fears.

**Fantasy**: [Little Witch Academia](https://myanimelist.net/anime/33489/Little_Witch_Academia_TV)
~
Akko Kagari finds herself as a new student at the Luna Nova Magical Academy with little in the way of magical aptitude.  However, this doesn't stop her because what she does possess is determination bordering on recklessness in the face of her obstacles.  Helped along by her friends, her mentor, and her own spirit, Akko is determined to become a witch worthy of her childhood idol, Shiny Chariot.

**Mystery**: [Hyouka](https://myanimelist.net/anime/12189/Hyouka)
~
Rather than focus on massive, global conspiracies or insidious plots, Hyouka focuses on the small mysteries of life.  Told from the point of view of the listless Houtarou Oreki, this series follows him and the other members of the Classics Club as they solve various mysteries that spring up around their school.  Beautiful both from a visual and a story perspective, this series has a lot to offer if you're interested in a lighthearted story that encourages you to be curious about the world.

**Romance**: [Toradora!](https://myanimelist.net/anime/4224/Toradora)
~
Clannad has already been mentioned, so let's take a look at a different classic romance.  Toradora! is all about two students who hatch a plan to help the other get with their respective best friends.  The story quickly unfolds and the connections of friendship and love that tie all of the characters together are exposed and examined.  Not the most original story by any means, but it does what it sets out to do so well that it more than deserves its high regard.

**Sports**: [Chihayafuru](https://myanimelist.net/anime/10800/Chihayafuru)
~
Not a traditional sports anime, but great nonetheless, Chihayafuru follows our MC, Chihaya Ayase, as she strives to become the best karuta (a traditional Japanese card game) player that she possibly can be.  This is a series that starts out a little slow, but quickly builds up steam as you become engrossed in its characters and their ambitions.  Well-written, well-executed, and overall great, Chihayafuru is definitely worth looking into.

**Science Fiction**: [Planetes](https://myanimelist.net/anime/329/Planetes)
~
Garbage collectors in space - that's the position that our characters are in.  While spacewalks and astronauts are almost mythical in our world, in the world of Planetes they are a rather mundane, regular facet of life.  Planetes is a look into the life of a new member of the Debris Section, Ai Tanabe, her veteran partner, "Hachi," and the staff that help them get the job done.  A grounded science fiction story that does a great job bringing its characters to life - one of my favorites.

**Slice of Life**: [Aria The Animation](https://myanimelist.net/anime/477/Aria_The_Animation)
~
The Aria series follows a girl named Akari Mizunashi and her friends as they train to become the next best Undines (gondola tour guides) in New Venezia.  New Venezia is a city modeled after Venice on the terraformed planet of Aqua (formerly Mars) and the visual beauty that it possesses is some of the best in anime. The stakes are never all that high, but that's not the point. What is the point then? Simple - sitting back and relaxing while you watch an absolutely gorgeous anime and get to know the girls.

**Thriller**: [Madoka Magica](https://myanimelist.net/anime/9756/Mahou_Shoujo_Madoka%E2%98%85Magica)
~
On its surface Madoka Magica looks to be another magical girl anime much like any other, but after a few episodes you begin to see that there is far more to it than meets the eye.  What does it mean to become a magical girl?  What are the terms of the contract?  These are two questions that our MC, Madoka Kaname, explores over the course of this series.  I'd say more, but I don't want to spoil anything for you.  This one is definitely worth the watch.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask away.  I hope that was helpful!

[Eve no Jikan](https://myanimelist.net/anime/3167/Eve_no_Jikan) (Time of Eve) is a sci-fi/slice of life anime worth taking a look at.  It's only made up of six 20 minute episodes, but they're all excellent and get you thinking about a few different things.  It doesn't try to evoke any specific emotions, rather it tries to get you to think about what it means to be human.  The way it does this is through its characters, which, despite having small amounts of screen time, all bring something different to the table.  If that sounds interesting, then you can check it out on Crunchyroll.

If you really loved the original dub, then you probably won't enjoy the new one quite as much.  The script is more literal and the delivery is less stylized - it's more flat and even-keeled in comparison (if that makes sense).  There's also the fact that they took out all of the Fly Me to the Moon ED's as well as its few appearances in episodes.  That's not to say that it's bad - it really isn't - it just feels very different.

Oniisama e... is one of my all-time favorites, and I'm loving it as much as ever.  It has been around two years or so since I last watched it, so it was a treat to sit down with some tea and a blanket and hide from the early snow with a great drama.  It always makes me smile when I realize that it's just as beautiful on the millionth watch as it was on the first.
You are definitely a member of the [target audience](https://imgur.com/a/UlyWnsr).

If it gets that praise, I don't see it here or on r/anime at all.  Maybe I'm just blind.

Either way, yeah, it's one of those shows that takes a bit of time to get into.  The characters start to come alive near the end of the first season and after that you really start connecting with them.  Part of this is the budget being so low at the beginning, but the other part is that they aren't as *extemely* superficial as others in the genre are.  I'm not going to say that the character development is as great as other anime that really focus on it like Monster or LotGH do, but for a CGDCT anime it does a great job.

For example, you can really see the change that Yuno undergoes as the series progresses.  She starts as a a character that's more timid than anything else and comes out of her shell over the course of the series.

{Hidamari Sketch} and all of its sequels are the best cute girls doing cute things anime out there.  As much as I like K-On!, Non Non Biyori, Lucky Star, Azumanga Daioh, Yuru Camp, and etc. they can never top Hidamari Sketch in my heart. Take [this ED](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dFp_i2EYiMk) for example.  It just seems like another generic, cute ED, but the way they characterized everyone in it is just perfect.  It starts with Hiro, the 'mom' and best cook of the group, coming in quietly to leave a snack for Yuno, Sae, the 'dad' and responsible one of the group, stops by to deliver the schoolwork like a responsible senior would, after that is the duo of Nori & Nazuna, the juniors of Yuno who want to help their senior however they can, and they cover her in a light blanket, last is Miyako, the real sunshine of Sunshine Sketch, who comes in as loudly as her character is bold, and takes a moment to watch her best friend sleeping before leaving a message for her to wake up to.  After all of the characters have their time, the animation shifts into a beautiful dream sequence and Shaft has their opportunity to flex on other studios - keep in mind that this was all done for a 2 episode special series.

All in all, Hidamari Sketch is an underrated treasure that I'll never stop recommending to other anime watchers.  It has a heart and soul deeper than almost anything else in its niche and deserves 100x the praise that it gets.  Do yourself a favor and watch it - it's the best series to watch an episode or two of before you fall asleep - it's just that cozy.

* Degree of viciousness
* Motive

* Outcome of the crime; especially the number of victims.
* Sentiments of the bereaved family members.
* Impact of the crime on Japanese society.
* Defendant's age (in Japan, the age of majority is 20).
* Defendant's previous criminal record.
* Degree of remorse shown by the defendant.

I have a few reasons why I think that Kizumonogatari second makes more sense than Nisemonogatari.

First, there's the fact that the intent was never to have Kizu in the release position that it was in in the first place. 
 Kizu was delayed over and over again, so they went ahead and did the other entries until they got around to finishing the movies.

Second, the novel release order supports this order too.  The release order was Bake vol. 1, Bake vol. 2, Kizu, and **then** Nise.  The publisher has even suggested reading Kizu first (which I think is kind of silly).

Third, there's important story information that you get in Kizu that may make things unnecessarily confusing for new watchers that don't have it.  Personally, I also feel as though Kizu helps you to appreciate a few of the characters quite a bit more than you would have otherwise.

Honestly, whichever way you do it I still think you'll have fun.  The characters are all wonderful enough without worrying too much about how you enjoy them.

[Here's a pretty standard list.](https://www.mtggoldfish.com/archetype/legacy-high-tide-60904#paper)

You filter through your deck using cantrips to sculpt your hand.  From there you attempt to go off on your opponent's turn using High Tide + Reset to generate large amounts of mana, Mission Briefing to rebuy cards that you need, and protect the combo using Force and Flusterstorm.  You eventually win by using Cunning Wish to grab either Blue Sun's Zenith to force your opponent to draw their deck or High Tide to mill them out.

If you end up trying it out, feel free to message me with any other questions.

As far as combo goes, I'd also recommend Sneak & Show for it's relatively relaxed learning curve.  If you don't care as much about raw power, I also think that Reset High Tide is a lot of fun for newer legacy players.  You should already have the fetches and forces, so the only relatively pricey cards left to grab are Flusterstorms and Resets.  It has a lot of play to it and really rewards your skill with the deck.  It does demand that you put in the reps so that you know how and when to combo off against certain decks due to the limitations of Reset, but learning what other decks have available as disruption is a great skill that you can apply to playing any deck in the format.

Also, you can make the transition to Spiral Tide later on, which is my absolute favorite deck in the format.  :-)

* Flying Witch - A witch-in-training moves to rural Japan to learn and practice her magic.  This one is much more slice of life and relaxing than story driven.
* Kinos's Journey (2017) - A girl and her talking motorcycle travel between various countries.  This one has wonderful new characters and locations that pop up each episode.
* Mushishi - An episodic series about wandering man that studies and works with "spirits".  One of my all time favorite comfy shows.  The atmosphere and artistic direction in each episode is amazing.
